title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative: DİSK Confederation (Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Türkiye), the Turkish Union of Commerce, Cooperatives, Education, Office and Fine Arts (TEZ-KOOP-IS Union), Turkey's Journalists Union (TGS Union), Trade Union in Textile and Garment (OZIPLIK-IS Union), All Municipal and Public Services Worker's Trade Union (HIZMET IS), and Food Workers' Union (ÖZ GIDA-IS Union) adopted a "Zero Tolerance to Violence Policy Document” in 2022, in line with Convention No. 190. The document includes commitments to eliminating violence and harassment in their own structures and to putting workplace violence and harassment on social dialogue agendas. The capacity of trade unions including DISK TEKSTİL Union (Textile trade union), TEZKOOP-IS Union, OZ-SAGLIK-IS Union (trade union for health workers), OZIPLIK-IS Union, the Cement, Ceramics, Soil and Glass Industry Workers Union (OZTOPRAK-IS Union), was strengthened through awareness and sensitization workshops. As a result, the organisations were able to include provisions on violence and harassment in collective agreements with some of the companies where they are organised. Special measures to eliminate work-related violence and harassment, including gender-based violence and harassment, support services for the survivors have been included in such collective agreements. In 2023, Antalya Metropolitan Municipality adopted a “Zero Tolerance to Violence” policy in line with Convention No. 190, becoming the first local authority in Türkiye to take political action on eliminating violence and harassment in the world of work. This workplace policy commits the Municipality to eliminating workplace violence and harassment and developing support systems in its own premises where over 2500 women work. The policy has been the result of negotiation and collaboration with the Federation of Women’s Associations of Turkey (TKDF). With financial support from the Government of Sweden, the ILO established a multi-stakeholder “Advocacy and Policy initiative” for the promotion and implementation of Convention No. 190 in 2022. This multi-stakeholder initiative comprised a coalition of trade union confederations, trade unions, civil society organisations, private sector companies, other UN Agencies, and academia in 2022. Through this multi-stakeholder initiative, the ILO delivered two experience sharing fora and four workshops on zero tolerance to violence policy documents for workers’ organizations, private sector partners and a civil society organisation (CSO). Workers’ representatives’ awareness and capacity on Convention No. 190 were also enhanced, including through a peer-to-peer experience sharing forum in 2022. The ILO delivered tailor made trainings on gender equality and international labour standards with a special focus on Convention No. 190 to trade unions. In collaboration with ITC-ILO, the ILO delivered "Ending Violence and Harassment in the World of Work: A Training for Change-Makers" training of trainers to 31 participants from the trade union confederations, public employees' union confederations, CSO's and academia in 2022. The ILO provided technical training to the Federation of Women’s Associations of Turkey (TKDF), resulting in the TKDF’s increased capacity on Convention No. 190 and their subsequent role as advocates for the elimination of violence and harassment in the world of work. Together with the TKDF, the ILO provided technical support to the development of the Zero Tolerance to Violence document adopted by the Antalya Metropolitan Municipality. The ILO provided technical support to social partners in their negotiation efforts towards the inclusion of provisions on violence and harassment in their collective agreements.

description.narrative:
Public Services Employees Union of Türkiye which is affiliated member of Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Türkiye made an amendment in its statute with the aim of gender mainstreaming in the union and the organised workplaces in 2022. During the 2022-23 biennium the ILO has been following the organizational road maps which were prepared through the participatory gender audits on policies, programmes and actions of the 23 workers' and employers' organizations. One of the common recommendations for filling the gender gap in the world of work is the inclusion of clauses on gender equality in political documents of the social partners.
The ILO delivered constant mentorship to social partners on the implementation of the roadmaps. These roadmaps underlined the importance of the women representation and leadership in the workers' and employers' organizations for increasing decent working conditions of women.
The ILO compiled data for determining the potential actions that could be taken to increase women's representation at decision making bodies of the social partners. These potentials actions were also discussed and finalized at the "Women's Representation at Decision Making Bodies of the Social Partners Workshop", where the representatives and/or experts from the women committees or units of the workers' and employers' organizations and the women organizations participated in May 2023.
Aiming to increase the workers' and employers' organizations' capacities on international labour standards and women's employment, by the financial support of Sweden, ILO delivered the 'Current Situation of Women's Employment in the World and in Türkiye', 'I Support Equality', 'Legislative and Structural Framework on Gender Equality' and 'Advocacy' digital trainings with the participation of 737 representatives of the social partners and public institutions in 2022&2023.

description.narrative:
The ILO, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and The Union of Municipalities of Türkiye (UMT) built a consensus on the ‘legislative recommendation document’ for enabling proper legal background for delivery of standard and qualified, widespread, and accessible early childcare and education (ECCE) services via municipalities in 2022 and 2023. The Ministry of National Education, Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change and the Ministry of Family and Social Services stated their commitment for related legal amendments during advocacy meetings on adoption of this paper which was prepared via a consultation process with participation of the representatives of municipalities, private sector, related public institutions, CSOs, workers’ and employers’ organizations in 2022. “Supporting Women’s Employment through Institutional Collaboration on Early Childhood Care and Education” report, prepared by the ILO and EBRD with the financial support of Sweden, revealed the need for standard and qualified, widespread, and accessible ECCE services via municipalities. Report underlined the widespread delivery of the ECCE services by the municipalities as one of the practices that should be scaled up. The ILO realized the need for overcoming legal problems that are faced by the municipalities during this process and a new collaborative initiative between the ILO, EBRD and the UMT started with the aim of development of ‘legislative recommendation document’ for enabling proper legal background.
ILO enabled involvement of the constituents into the development processes of the document. The women’s access to the work opportunities via accessible and widespread ECCE services perspective is reflected in the document. ILO especially emphasized the “5R Framework for Decent Care Work: recognize, reduce and redistribute unpaid care work; reward paid care work by promoting more and decent work for care workers; and guarantee care workers’ representation, social dialogue and collective bargaining” and underlined the related international standards such as C156 during both development and advocacy procedures of the ‘legislative recommendation paper’.
In line with report above, ILO collaborates with municipalities to facilitate ECCE to become operational through technical and financial support. The municipality will be selected following a feasibility assessment which will focus on the most refugee-populated districts in the project provinces. ECCE aims to provide child-care service to working-aged women and men with the duty of care so that they can benefit from skills development programmes, and employment services and are referred to employment.
